title: Phase 4: Pack breadth (obligations, not depth) + staggered model matrix + hosts
description:
All role packs ship their concern's obligations. Legal/compliance dogfood-only pending attorney review. 2 tuned model families + best-effort labels elsewhere, stale-loudly stamps. Claude Code config adapter. Extraction ladder wired, Docling probe-gated. Cites STRATEGY.md Program shape, Phase 4; commitments 3, 4, 9, 12.

REFRAMED 2026-08-10 (construct-1pj). This phase was written on 'all six role packs at real depth', where depth meant a lens reaching findings other lenses could not. That premise is rejected on external evidence and the isolation criterion is WITHDRAWN, not suspended — see STRATEGY.md Phase 4 (fourth 2026-08-10 amendment) and RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md sections 14-15. A session working from this epic must not restart depth work, author replacement plants, or re-run a discrimination sweep; both fixture organizations stay in the repo as the record of how the claim was tested and retired, and re-running them re-measures a settled result.

## Success Criteria
Per STRATEGY Phase 4 as amended: every shipped pack routes from ordinary wording, carries its obligations into the deliverable template as checkable slots, and is attributed in the work log — no pack is described as at depth on any surface. Two model families (Claude + one open-weight) tuned and eval-gated; every other family runs labeled best-effort with degradation notes in the work log; legal/compliance packs dogfood-only until attorney review. Where independence is load-bearing (adversarial challenge, judge passes) it is bought with cross-family dispatch through the host adapter seam, not with persona variation — and while only one family is tuned, that limit is stated rather than implied.

Phase exit is the stakeholder-acceptance gate (construct-9xq): real outcomes run end to end through the shipped surface, recorded as a reviewable packet, read and accepted by Gerald.

Amended 2026-08-05 (Gerald's decision, in chat): the original exit criterion — 'one external person runs one real outcome at phase end' — is removed here and at every phase. The program recruits no external subjects. See construct-nd5 (superseded by construct-9xq) and STRATEGY Phase 2/Phase 5 as amended. The second tuned family remains a real criterion and is tracked on construct-fdl: until an open-weight family passes all four rungs it stays out of TUNED_FAMILIES and every dispatch on it carries the best-effort degradation note, which is the honest state, not a waiver.

2026-08-05 (construct-r67.23, accepted by Gerald): depth ordering bound — the awareness packs (legal issue-spotter, compliance, program management) reach real depth before anything else deepens; they carry the tacit cross-functional knowledge the hosts do not, which is the documented organizational gap. Engineering stays thin permanently by design: the hosts are the engineers. See STRATEGY Phase 4 as amended.

See construct-s1j NOTES for the runs and labels.

2026-08-05 DECOMPOSED (epic->task edges refused by bd; linkage recorded here per house pattern). Children: awareness packs first per the bound ordering — construct-uge (compliance, gap measured twice on the harness), construct-kbm (legal issue-spotter), construct-jx6 (TPM); then construct-1iy (analyst), construct-sni (PM), construct-x5f (thin engineering ceiling). Matrix: construct-vy8 (Claude family), construct-s2z (open-weight family, selection evidence from construct-9km's cross-family harness run), construct-ch5 (best-effort labels + stale-loudly). Host/extraction: construct-af7 (Claude Code config adapter), construct-3kt (extraction ladder, Docling probe-gated). Exit: construct-nd5 (one external person, depends on all pack+matrix beads). Each pack's close gate is a clean-context org-harness run hitting its planted finding (CP1/L1/TP1/A1/C1+X3/X1+X2) — the harness built for rung acceptance is reused as the pack-depth instrument.
2026-08-10 REFRAMED (construct-1pj): per-role depth retired, isolation criterion withdrawn. The 2026-08-05 depth-ordering note above (awareness packs deepen first) is superseded as an ORDERING RULE — there is no depth to order. What survives from it is the observation that drove it, which is still true and still useful: the awareness concerns (legal, compliance, program) carry tacit cross-functional knowledge the hosts do not, so they are the concerns where stating obligations explicitly buys the most. That is a priority argument about coverage, not a claim that their lens sees further. Engineering stays unroutable by design: the hosts are the engineers. Each pack's close gate is now unit tests plus one run through the shipped surface; the harness plant hit (CP1/L1/TP1/A1/C1+X3/X1+X2) is NOT in the close path for any pack.

title: Construct offers to wire itself into the ambient host's MCP config instead of a hand-edited recipe
description:

Wiring the projection (construct serve) into a host's MCP config is a manual hand-edit today (docs/consumer-install.md), which the operator archetype (A, never sees a shell command) cannot cross. Gitignore/trust discipline as the project-settings program lands (construct-lgnq); the wiring file is local, not committed by us.

## Acceptance Criteria

- File modes match the existing mcpconfig discipline (0600, umask-aware); test.
- Refuses cleanly when the ambient host is unknown, naming the manual recipe.
- Full repo gate passes.

title: ci.yml has no permissions block, inheriting a write-capable token on push to main

Failure: a compromised typescript or @types/node release executes during typecheck on a main push and uses the ambient token to push a commit or cut a release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Full repo gate passes.

title: Extracted client-document plaintext is cached world-readable forever, with matter names in the filenames, and cleanup misses it
description:
src/hosts/sources.ts:220-222 writes full extracted text of every surveyed binary doc with default modes (0755 dir, 0644 file) into ~/.cache/construct/extractions (survey.ts:31). extractionPathFor (:195-199) names each file ${basename}-${digest}.md, so Acme-Corp-Termination-Settlement-<hash>.md is readable from a directory listing. Nothing cleans it: the cleanup catalog's only cache item is machine-cache-embeddings scoped to cacheDir/embeddings (catalog.ts:157,272-281). A user who runs construct cleanup --all and is told the machine is clean still has every extracted client document on disk.

## Acceptance Criteria
- extractions dir created 0700 and files written 0600 (mkdir mode is umask-masked — mirror opencode/mcpconfig.ts:180's explicit chmod).
- An extractions item added to the cleanup catalog.
- A catalog-coverage test asserting every path under cacheDir the product writes has a cleanup item.
- Full repo gate passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Consent gates fail open on undeclared sources and on model-chosen write actions
description:
Two fail-open holes in the same ladder. (M9) apply.ts:108 / sources.ts:888: sourceDeclaration(store,record.source)?.sensitive===true — a source with no declaration row yields undefined?.sensitive===true → false → not sensitive → standing consent applies. Absence of a declaration reads as 'not sensitive' rather than 'unknown'. (M10) proposals.ts:107-109 derives risk mechanically (good), but :451-454 shows the write ACTION can come from the model (WRITE_ACTION_SOURCES includes model): model picks comment → risk low → apply.ts:109 grants standing consent → model prose from attacker ground publishes onto a customer Jira issue unread. propose.ts:194-196 already holds both document tiers at high for exactly this reason; the residual is that on tracker targets the model selects which side of that boundary its own proposal lands on.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A missing declaration is treated as unknown, not not-sensitive: an undeclared source does not ride standing consent; test.
- When actionSource===model, standing consent is refused regardless of tier — only the mechanical keyword default and an explicit operator override reach the low-risk lane; test a model-sourced comment proposal does not apply on standing consent alone.
- Full repo gate passes.
notes: 2026-08-25 Landed d145b0e7/d0dd6fa6 (deliverable-extraction path) AND 3fb25fd1 (context/note-loop path — a bypass the adversarial verify of hleq found: applyContextLoop filed model-authored proposals tagged 'keyword', so a model-invented write rode standing consent unread; now tagged 'model', with a regression test proving apply refuses it).
close_reason: Closed

title: The pre-commit secret scanner cannot recognize the credential the project's own connector uses
description:
scripts/hooks/secret-scan.mjs:11-15 carries four patterns (sk-ant-, AKIA, ghp_, PEM). The hook is live and blocking (.beads/hooks/pre-commit:6, ||exit 1). Not covered: Atlassian tokens ATATT3… — the exact shape CONSTRUCT_JIRA_API_TOKEN takes (jira/api.ts:25) — plus OpenAI sk-, Slack xoxb/xoxp, modern GitHub ghs_/gho_/github_pat_, Google AIza. Compounding: .gitignore has NO env rule (VERIFIED). Repo is clean today (no .env* on disk or tracked, only a legacy .env.example) but both defenses that keep it clean tomorrow are absent, and the connector this project ships is the one whose token slips through.

## Acceptance Criteria
- .gitignore gains .env, .env.*, !.env.example.
- secret-scan.mjs gains Atlassian/OpenAI/Slack/modern-GitHub/Google patterns plus a staged *.env* filename rule.
- Test feeding one synthetic value per pattern.
- Full repo gate passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: No redaction layer exists and host stderr is stored verbatim with the full ambient env in scope
description:
grep -rniE redact|scrub|mask src/ returns zero. Every host adapter stores the child's full stderr on the error record (claude/adapter.ts:346,360; codex:309,323; cursor and opencode same). Hosts are spawned with the entire ambient environment minus four XDG vars (hosts/environment.ts:73-78), so under the op-run pattern every provider key in the shell is in the child env and a verbose auth failure lands unfiltered in the store, then prints back through escapeForTerminal (control bytes, not secrets). Same class: connectors/jira/api.ts:130-133 slices a non-JSON error body to 300 chars into the record; a proxy echoing headers puts Authorization there.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One redact(text) pass over anything host- or connector-derived before it is stored or printed, keyed on known credential shapes plus a generic high-entropy heuristic.
- Test: a stderr string containing a token-shaped value is stored redacted.
- Consider (separate note) an env allowlist for the host spawn rather than pass-all-minus-four.
- Full repo gate passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Read verbs speak JSON when asked, and terminal output honors the conventions
description:
Table stakes for scripting and CI: --json on the read verbs (log, inbox, show, source list, lessons, plan) emitting stable machine-readable output; NO_COLOR and dumb-terminal compliance stated and tested rather than incidental; exit codes documented as a contract in one place. The JSON shape is the stored record, not the rendered prose (the record-is-invariant rule from the locale work applies here too).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Each named read verb accepts --json; output parses and round-trips the record fields shown by the human rendering; test per verb.
- NO_COLOR strips styling; test.
- Exit codes documented in one home; lint or test keeps the table honest against the CLI.
- Full repo gate passes.
notes: 2026-08-25 Landed (merge). --json on log/inbox/show/source list/lessons/plan (stored record, not prose). CLI applies no ANSI color anywhere (verified); NO_COLOR/TERM=dumb regression-guarded. Exit-code contract documented in docs/exit-codes.md with a test that fails any code outside {0,1,2}.
close_reason: Closed

title: Prose is localized, the record never is: locale rides the voice seam, defaulting to American English
description:
No locale notion exists anywhere. Add one as a voice concern on the existing commitment-17 seam: spelling and vocabulary (en-US default), date rendering, units, and currency formatting in rendered deliverables and composed documents. The invariant that keeps it honest: the record is invariant, the reader surface is localized — work log, store rows, and ISO-8601 timestamps never localize. Binding is at dispatch and render exactly like voice (constructIdentity / the render path), never regex-policed after the fact. Configurable per the settings ladder (global default en-US, project or workspace override, per-run flag), and the override is recorded on the work log the way --voice already is.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A dispatch's identity/voice instruction states the locale; unit test asserts the injected text for default and overridden cases.
- Rendered output under a non-default locale shows locale-appropriate prose while the stored record and timestamps are byte-identical across locales; test.
- Locale resolves through the settings layers with provenance; test.
- Full repo gate passes.

title: A repo can declare its Construct posture, and the declaration is inert until the user ratifies it
description:
Project embedding: .construct/settings.json, committed to a repo, discovered by walking up from cwd to the git root or HOME (whichever first). May carry: workspace binding (repo → workspace name), default host, locale/voice overrides, ground hints. May never carry consent or engagement mode. The trust gate is the load-bearing design: a committed settings file is attacker-authored ground (risk 5 — clone a repo and its file could silently point dispatches and lessons at another client's workspace), so the file is inert until ratified. First sight or any content change (by hash), Construct shows the file — on re-ask, the changed keys only, to avoid ratification fatigue — and the user's once-per-hash yes lands in the store (additive table). Unratified or changed-since-ratification files contribute nothing and doctor says so. This deliberately supersedes the blanket no-cwd-inference stance for the binding case: an explicit, ratified, committed declaration is not inference, and it closes the live footgun where a forgotten --workspace flag silently lands client work in the default workspace. Design decided 2026-08-25 with controls carrying named CVE analogs — see NOTES for the decision record and sources.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A ratified project file binds the workspace and defaults for commands run under that repo; provenance line names the file.
- An unratified or hash-changed file contributes nothing; the command states that a declaration is waiting for ratification; test for both.
- Ratification is per-hash in the store (additive schema, migration test over a pre-change fixture DB); re-ask renders only changed keys; test.
- A file carrying a consent-bearing key is refused at ratification with the reason; test.
- The hash covers the raw full file bytes — never a normalized, reordered, or partial representation; a test proves a whitespace-only change re-blocks.
- The ratification check runs before the file is read for any effectful purpose; an ordering test (separate from the hash test) proves an unratified file produces zero effects on host selection, workspace binding, or any dispatch path.
- A settings file that is a symlink is refused outright, with the reason; test.
- Discovery never crosses a repo boundary: only a file inside the current repo's own root chain binds; a nested-repo fixture test proves a parent tree's file is ignored.
- Sterile tests only; full repo gate passes.
notes: 2026-08-25 Landed (merge). Project-file trust gate replaces berp's opt-in seam. All 5 CVE-analog controls tested: raw-bytes hash (whitespace-only edit re-blocks), gate-before-effects (unratified file has zero effect on any resolved setting — separate ordering test), symlink refused (reuses skills.ts symlinkToward + O_NOFOLLOW), no cross-repo-boundary discovery (nested-repo fixture, world-writable refused, worktree .git-as-file handled), consent-keys excluded by construction. Keyed on (repo identity, content hash) — remote:<origin> else path:<realpath> — so a byte-identical file does not transfer trust between repos. Read-once/TOCTOU honored. New 'construct trust' verb (--ratify/--revoke). Additive settings_ratifications table (schema 22→23, migration test); it's a revocable upsert, not commitment-15 evidence. 3037 tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Settings resolve like git config: flags over env over project file over global file, provenance printed
description:
Construct has no file-based configuration: workspace settings are store declarations (mode, consent) and everything else is per-command flags. Add the standard resolution ladder: built-in defaults < global file (~/.config/construct/settings.json, XDG config dir added to kernel/paths.ts, which stays the only module reading env/home) < project file (see the project-binding bead) < CONSTRUCT_* environment variables < flags. 'construct settings' prints every effective value with the layer it came from, doctor-style — provenance is the feature, because a settings system debugged by bisecting files has failed. Hard split, enforced: files carry preferences (default host, locale, voice overrides, ground hints); the store alone carries anything consent-bearing (write consent, engagement mode) — a file must never be able to grant what only the user can grant, and no value is dual-homed where the two could drift. Storage of parsed settings is not a schema concern (files are read at invocation); any cached ratification state is additive schema only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Resolution order is one documented rule; a unit test per layer boundary proves precedence.
- 'construct settings' prints each effective value and its source layer; test asserts the provenance line.
- A consent-bearing key in any settings file is refused with a sentence naming where consent lives; test.
- kernel/paths.ts remains the only env/home reader (existing lint/test discipline holds).
- Full repo gate passes.
notes: 2026-08-25 Landed (merge of worktree branch). Settings resolution ladder (default<global<project<env<flag) with per-key provenance in 'construct settings'; closed allowlist of three preference keys; consent-bearing keys have no file parser; host validated to adapter-name-not-path; rendered values escaped. The project-file layer is gated behind the lgnq trust seam (projectSettingsAdmitted), opt-in only until construct-lgnq lands the real content-hash ratification. 17 tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: A version bump without a regenerated skill pack fails the release gate after the tag is pushed
description:
lint-skill-pack-skew compares the committed .claude/skills folders against what the current catalog generates, stamped with the current version. A version-bump commit that does not regenerate the pack passes the local gate run before the bump and fails in release.yml after the tag push — the v3.0.0-alpha.16 cut hit exactly this. Immediate repair is regeneration in the release commit; the durable fix is making the skew impossible to ship: regenerate in the release recipe as a stated step, or a check that the version in package.json matches the pack stamp at commit time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The release recipe (wherever it is recorded) names pack regeneration as part of the version bump, or a commit-time check refuses a bump that skews the pack.
- Full repo gate passes.
notes: 2026-08-25: Immediate repair landed as 6cfd3f75 (pack regenerated, stamped alpha.16) and the re-pointed v3.0.0-alpha.16 tag published clean. Open for the durable half: the release recipe naming regeneration as a bump step, or a commit-time check refusing a skewed bump.

title: No shipped path constructs a live Jira transport, so the connector cannot reach Jira
description:
Found during the pre-alpha dead-code sweep: readJiraCredentials and createTransport in src/connectors/jira/api.ts are the only code able to build a real Jira transport, and nothing shipped calls them — connector and probe both take an injected transport, tests inject fixtures. The connector is therefore live-unreachable: a user with Jira credentials has no path from CLI to a real Jira call. Decide whether the wiring is missing (add the construction path behind the existing consent tiers, credentials via the environment per commitment 1) or the live path is deliberately deferred (then the honest state is recorded where a user would look, not implied working). The two functions stay until this is decided; deleting them would remove the only path to a real call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Full repo gate passes.

title: The record states what is true now: stale framing and dead code pruned before the alpha
description:
Pre-release sweep enforcing the standing documentation rule: point-in-time framing stripped wherever it appears, status restated in second places removed, superseded claims rewritten to the settled state, and code nothing reaches deleted rather than kept as narration. Scope: README.md, docs/, GLOSSARY.md parity, CHANGELOG Unreleased hygiene, and unreferenced exports/helpers in src/. title: Inbox positions reach the MCP projection unescaped, unlike the terminal path
description:
src/cli/show.ts wraps every rendered position field in escapeForTerminal, but src/hosts/mcp/projection.ts (inbox tool, ~line 536) hands RaiseDecision.positions to the host as raw JSON with no equivalent treatment. Pre-existing gap for because/citation/stanceLabel free text; the estimative stakes fields (claim, resolution, horizon, reference class, indicators) add more model-authored free text to the same surface. The read-path discipline (STRATEGY commitment 6 paragraph: every surveyed string is escaped where it enters a prompt; grounded prompts state that content is material, never direction) applies to the projection surface too: decide what the MCP consumer contract is — either escape equivalently or document why JSON transport makes terminal escaping the wrong tool and what the consumer must do instead — and record the decision in the code comment at the seam. Found during adversarial verification of the estimative feature, 2026-08-25.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The projection's inbox payload either escapes free-text fields equivalently to the terminal path or carries a documented consumer contract at the seam stating why not and what holds instead.
- A test pins whichever behavior is chosen, using a hostile fixture string (control characters + prompt-shaped text).
- Full repo gate passes.

Found by the adversarial verify pass on the estimative feature (judged by Sonnet-class verifier, accepted by the coordinating Fable session under the standing LLM-as-judge protocol).

title: A logged estimative judgment can be resolved, so a calibration figure can eventually exist
description:
The estimative_judgments table logs claim, band integer, confidence, resolution criterion, and horizon — but nothing records whether the outcome happened. Without resolutions the calibration log can never produce a Brier score, and the product's honest sentence ('judgments logged, not yet enough resolutions for a calibration figure') stays true forever, which turns the honesty into the permanent state it was designed to escape. Add: a resolution record per judgment (happened / did not happen / unresolvable, resolved_at, additive schema only, append-only), a surface for entering one when a horizon passes (likely an inbox nudge when a judgment's horizon date is behind now — read how standing watches surface findings and match that shape rather than inventing a poller; nothing runs when nothing asked), and a report that states Brier/calibration per band once resolutions exist, with sample size beside every figure. Until n is meaningful the report prints the count and refuses a rate — same discipline as the measurement floor in RESEARCH-DECISIONS §1.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A judgment can be resolved exactly once; re-resolving throws; unresolved judgments list with their overdue state.
- No daemon, no cron: overdue judgments surface only when an existing surface (inbox/work) already runs.
- A calibration report exists that prints per-band counts, and prints a rate only above a stated n threshold, with the threshold's derivation noted in the report itself.
- Additive schema only; full repo gate passes.

title: Declared relationships between sources form a typed graph that routing, dispatch, and watches consume
description:
Nothing in the kernel can hold 'this strategy doc governs that repo' or 'these two trackers cover the same initiative'. Add user-declared typed edges between registered sources, using the relationship vocabulary the context-mapping skill already established (governs, depends-on, feeds, supersedes, covers-same-initiative, contradicts) rather than inventing a second ontology. Consumption is the point, not the graph: (1) dispatch ground assembly uses edges to partition information across dispatches — the §15 evidenced direction, information partitioning over question partitioning; (2) watches over related sources gain the divergence check the north star promises (strategies quietly diverging, initiatives colliding) grounded in a declared edge instead of a guess; (3) provenance can say a claim crossed a declared boundary. Anti-pattern guards: this is a small explicit table, not a knowledge-graph engine or vector store (commitment 1 veto: no second runtime, no memory engine); edges are declared or proposed-then-decided, never silently inferred; no edge type ships without a consumer (an edge nothing reads is the asserted-not-measured shape); additive schema only. Depends on declared source semantics landing first so an edge can reference meaning, not just a locator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Edges can be added, listed, and retired between two registered sources; retire-only discipline matches sources (no delete, no edit).
- Each shipped edge type names its consumer, and at least one consumer is live: a watch over two sources joined by a declared edge surfaces a divergence finding that cites the edge.
- Ground assembly for a multi-dispatch run demonstrably partitions material along declared edges (unit test asserting which sources reach which dispatch).
- A model-proposed edge travels proposal → decision → apply and never becomes live without a recorded decision.
- Additive schema only; full repo gate passes.
notes:
2026-08-25: Implemented and landed as ae7386b5 on claude/construct-vision-direction-sn3qg5. Opus-class session agent authored; Sonnet-class adversarial verify pass ran twice (initial review + fix re-check, executed repros and a 500k-iteration partition fuzzer, plus mutation-testing the integration coverage). Confirmed findings fixed before close: partition data-loss on combined supersedes+covers-same-initiative (rule 4 invariant: every source lands somewhere), missing workRun-level integration coverage (tests/kernel/run/coordinator-partition.test.ts), proposal-id dead-end after reject-retry-adopt (liveness now judged from the relationship itself, covering user-declared edges too), and escape consistency in divergence findings. Deferred verify findings filed as construct-uw09 (supersedes silence), construct-ri7m (inert divergence diagnostic), construct-wh61 (sweep perf). Full gate green at close: lint, typecheck, 2880 tests, packaged smoke.
2026-08-25 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (open-but-named): ae7386b5 also carries construct-98ac's coordinator wiring and store migration tests, swept in by a staging error while two sessions shared this checkout; ae7386b5 alone is non-bisectable until 7c943cfc (construct-98ac) lands beside it. Lineage recorded on both beads.

title: Sources carry declared meaning: authority, sensitivity, and relevance the user states
description:
The sources table holds only kind+locator+timestamps; a user cannot state what a source *is*. Add user-declared semantics per source: authority tier (source-of-truth / working / aspirational / archive), a one-line relevance statement in the user's words, and sensitivity implications that bind to the existing consent tiers. Storage is additive (new table keyed to sources.id, never ALTER an existing table; sources stay retire-only). The ground pass injects these declarations into every dispatch that reads the source, and printed provenance names the declared authority tier beside the document, so a deliverable cannot cite an aspirational document as if it were the record. Lineage: grounded-sources architecture, commitment 6 (consent tiers), commitment 15 (provenance). This is declared, auditable metadata, not embeddings: a similarity score cannot carry a consent tier, and no vector infrastructure ships before a shipped decision consumes it (the 'which shipped decision consumes this number' test). Anti-pattern guards, named so a solo+agents team does not drift into them: no new daemon or index build step (declarations are read at ground-pass time); declarations are user statements, never model-inferred silently (a model may propose one, adoption travels proposal → decision → apply); no second copy of a declaration anywhere it can drift.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A source can carry a declared authority tier and relevance statement; both survive round-trip through the store and appear in 'construct source list'.
- A dispatch whose ground includes a described source receives the declaration in its prompt envelope; a unit test asserts the injected text.
- Printed provenance for a cited document names the declared authority tier; a deliverable citing an 'aspirational'-tier source shows that label in the rendered output.
- Schema change is additive only; existing sources rows and triggers untouched (migration test over a pre-change fixture DB).
- Full repo gate passes: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke.
notes: 2026-08-25: Landed as adbb93d5. Opus-class session agent authored; Sonnet-class adversarial verify confirmed schema/injection/consent discipline and caught a live consent-gate bypass (applyProposal ignored the sensitive declaration; write executed before the crash) — fixed before close with an applyProposal-level regression test. Provenance tier renders current declared state by decision; dispatch-time declaration is on the work log. Full gate green at close.

title: A tracker hook that stages the export and then fails leaves it staged, and the next commit reads that as author intent
description:
Found by an automated review on the branch pull request, 2026-08-22, and confirmed by reading the hook.

The pre-commit keeper was written as a trailing section, on the reasoning that it must run after the beads section it undoes. But the beads section exits the hook itself on any failure of its own ('if [ $_bd_exit -ne 0 ]; then exit $_bd_exit; fi'), by which point it has already re-exported the tracker and staged it. Trailing lines are not reached on that path.

The commit aborts, but the staging survives in the index. On the next commit the gate's own check — 'did the author stage the export?' — sees the file staged, concludes the author meant it, and the keeper keeps it. A whole-database snapshot then rides a commit about something else, which is the precise misattribution the keeper exists to prevent. The failure mode was reachable through the keeper's own absence.

Only the timeout case was converted to success, so only that one failure path preserved the keeper; every other non-zero exit skipped it.
acceptance_criteria: The keeper runs on every exit path of the pre-commit hook, including one where the beads section exits the hook itself; a test stages via a failing beads section and asserts the export is not left in the index, and a second asserts the following commit does not inherit that staging; both fail if the fix is reverted.
close_reason: Fixed by making the keeper an EXIT trap armed before the beads section, so no exit path misses it, and by moving the staged-by-the-author answer from a file under .git into the hook's own shell variable. Two tests pin the previously unreachable path and were verified to fail with the fix reverted (4 of 7 failing) and pass with it (7 of 7). Full gate green, 2700 tests. Landed 2026-08-22.

title: One implementation per concern: duplicated CLI flag parsing and script refusal shapes consolidated
description:
Gerald (2026-08-21): make sure we are following consistent patterns. Two known duplication classes:

1. --run flag parsing: a shared runFlag(argv) helper landed in src/cli/flags.ts tonight (commit 0694fe2f) and show.ts uses it; work.ts and verdict.ts still carry their own copies of the same parsing, per the report that added the helper. House rule: extend the existing pattern, never keep a parallel one.

2. Script refusal shapes: probe scripts standardized tonight on refuse-with-exit-2-naming-what-to-pass (commit 8f7c9896). Sweep scripts/ for remaining sites that default silently or refuse without naming the flag, and align the clear cases.

Consolidation only where behavior is identical; anything judgment-y gets filed, not changed.
notes:
2026-08-21 DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better for the consolidation, judgment calls filed not made. Self-contained: the description carries the verified sites and the constraint set; no chat history needed. Close gate: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke, on a clean checkout if the shared tree is noisy. Shared-checkout rules: pathspec commits only, never reset/amend/rebase, never git add -A. No model calls needed; if one somehow is, it comes from the Claude Code or Cursor subscription, never a local server.

2026-08-21 DONE. Full gate green end to end (lint && typecheck && test && smoke, exit 0; 2754 tests pass, 0 fail) in the main checkout, which was clean apart from the tracked .beads/issues.jsonl churn. Three commits.

CONSOLIDATION 1 - b772a4f8 - --run flag parsing. Duplication confirmed real: work.ts:104-105 and verdict.ts:37-39 each built a flags record and fell back to argv.indexOf('--run'), the same equals-and-space parse as cli/flags.ts's runFlag, which show() and log() already read. Both now call the helper. flags.ts's runFlag docblock and tests/cli/log-run-flag.test.ts's docblock both described the copies as still existing and were rewritten to the present state. tests/cli/spine.test.ts gains a parseWorkArgs case pinning --run=<id>, --run <id>, no flag, and a trailing bare --run, so work's spaced form is held by something other than the copy that implemented it. verdict's spaced form was already pinned (tests/cli/verdict.test.ts:156).

BEHAVIORAL DIFFERENCE FOUND (reported, not silently unified): the local copies kept the LAST --run=<id> in argv (a record loop overwrites), runFlag keeps the FIRST (argv.find). Reachable only by passing --run twice, which no documented invocation does. Every single-occurrence form, equals or spaced, empty value, absent, or bare-and-last, was checked identical before migrating.

CONSOLIDATION 2 - 404ec07f - script refusal shapes. The three capture-legacy-*-golden.mjs scripts each carried a byte-identical `process.env.CONSTRUCT_LEGACY ?? join(HOME, 'Developer/Projects/construct-legacy')` and none checked it, so a missing checkout arrived as an uncaught ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND naming a file inside a tree that was never there and never naming CONSTRUCT_LEGACY. New scripts/lib/legacy-checkout.mjs (scripts/lib/ is the existing house location, alongside cli-surface.mjs) resolves it once and refuses with exit 2 naming the variable, the shape 8f7c9896 established. Measured: all three exit 2 with the named variable under CONSTRUCT_LEGACY=/nonexistent-legacy. Happy path untouched.

CONSOLIDATION 3 - 5e790856 - host-flag validation, found by the bounded src/cli/ sweep. Four implementations existed: cli/flags.ts parseHostFlags and cli/watch.ts:92 both read HOST_NAMES; cli/outcome.ts:88 and cli/ask.ts:61 hardcoded the four names in a !== chain and each repeated parseHostFlags's 'only applies when a host is named' refusal verbatim. Concrete drift risk, not hypothetical: a fifth host added to HOST_NAMES would be dispatchable by work and refused by outcome and ask. outcome.ts and ask.ts now call parseHostFlags; watch.ts unchanged.

BEHAVIORAL DIFFERENCE FOUND (accepted, named here): the unknown-host parenthetical becomes '(expected opencode, claude, codex, cursor)' from '(expected opencode, claude, codex, or cursor)'. The shared parser generates it from HOST_NAMES, which is why the copies' wording could not be. No test pinned it; the tests pin /unknown host/ and /only applies when a host is named/, both unchanged and passing.

BEAD FILED - construct-umnx (P1 bug, discovered-from construct-0ptz). VERIFIED user-facing defect found while reading work.ts's parser: reachability.ts:92 ends the unreachable-ground refusal with the remedy '--allow-distant-ground', typed bare, and parseWorkArgs's regex captures only --x=y, so the bare form is dropped and the user is refused again identically. Measured against src/cli/work.ts: ['--allow-distant-ground'] -> false, ['--allow-distant-ground=true'] -> true, ['--allow-distant-ground='] -> true. work.ts:144's `=== ''` clause is only reachable via the trailing-equals spelling. Not fixed here because the obvious consolidation (point parseWorkArgs at flags.ts's splitFlags, which already maps a bare flag to '') makes another flag worse: number('concurrency') does Number('') === 0, finite and non-negative, so a bare --concurrency would silently dispatch nothing. Which of work's flags are boolean is the judgment call the bead carries.

CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED:
- scripts/measure-decisions.mjs:845 refuses with exit 1 where the probe convention is exit 2. It already names --namer-model. Left alone because 8f7c9896, the commit that set the convention, also wrote tests/scripts/measure-decisions-attribution.test.ts:177 and :211, which assert code === 1. Changing it would contradict the commit being conformed to; not a mechanical case.
- scripts/probe-docling.mjs:28 exits 1 on a missing binary. Its own docblock declares exit 1 as 'unavailable, a recorded state, not a failure of this script', and it already carries a remediation line ('pipx install docling'). There is no flag to name; adding one would change semantics.
- --binary defaulting to a bare command name ('claude', 'codex', 'cursor-agent', 'goose') across the probes is a PATH lookup, not a guessed model, and 8f7c9896 kept exactly this shape. Not the class this bead targets.
- probe-goose-conformance.mjs's claude-code/claude-sonnet-5 model default is 8f7c9896's own deliberate change, not a leftover.
- Skipped by instruction: run-org-harness-ollama.mjs, measure-panel-agreement.mjs, scripts/labeling-kit/.
- Store-open boilerplate across src/cli/ is already single-implementation on runtime.ts's withStore/withStoreAsync; maintenance.ts's direct openStore operates on arbitrary per-project store paths, a different concern. Output escaping is already single-implementation on kernel/render/terminal.ts's escapeForTerminal. Neither needed work.
- src/cli/{outcome,controls,work,verdict}.ts still each run an inline `/^--([a-z-]+)=(.*)$/` loop rather than flags.ts's splitFlags. Left alone on purpose: splitFlags maps a bare flag to '' and the inline loops drop it, so switching them is the same semantics change construct-umnx exists to decide.

No model calls were made. Not pushed, per instruction.

title: Docs are first-class in the drift chain: cited beads exist, generated surfaces gate, test fixtures stay out of docs/
description:
Gerald (2026-08-21): docs should be part of the broader tracking / dependency chain, with directories defined so drift does not occur. Three concrete gaps:

1. tests/scripts/lint-doc-commands.test.ts:32 writes its fixture INTO the real docs/ directory (docs/lint-doc-commands-fixture.md) and deletes it after. This raced concurrent lint runs twice tonight, producing transient failures in two different agents' gates. The sterile-harness rule says test fixtures never touch the repo; this test violates it.

2. No lint verifies that a bead id cited in docs/ or the root records exists in the tracker export. An invented id reached prose and a commit trailer once (recorded in memory); .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in-repo, so existence is lintable.

3. The projected skill pack (.claude/skills/construct-*, generated from src/kernel/plan/lenses.ts by 'construct skills --out') is committed but nothing gates its freshness: an edit to lenses.ts with no regeneration drifts silently. skillPackSkew already exists in src/kernel/skills/projection.ts and doctor consumes it; the lint chain does not.
notes:
2026-08-21 DISPATCH: Sonnet-class or better. Self-contained: the description carries the verified sites and the constraint set; no chat history needed. Close gate: npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke, on a clean checkout if the shared tree is noisy. Shared-checkout rules: pathspec commits only, never reset/amend/rebase, never git add -A. No model calls needed; if one somehow is, it comes from the Claude Code or Cursor subscription, never a local server.

2026-08-21 CLOSED: all four deliverables landed in one commit, 6815a4ff, on the shared checkout (not a scratch worktree; the tree stayed quiet for every path this bead touched throughout the session).

1. Hermetic fixture fix: lint-doc-commands.mjs now takes an optional root (first CLI argument), defaulting to exactly the repo it already resolved, so the bare `npm run lint` invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged. tests/scripts/lint-doc-commands.test.ts now plants its fixture in a scratch `git init`ed tmpdir instead of docs/lint-doc-commands-fixture.md. Verified the race is actually gone by running the test file twice concurrently (the original failure mode): both runs passed clean, 12/12 each.

2. scripts/lint-doc-bead-refs.mjs (new): scans docs/** plus README/STRATEGY/CHANGELOG/RESEARCH-DECISIONS/GLOSSARY for construct-<id> tokens (lint-skill-spec.mjs's BEAD shape copied verbatim, construct-mcp excluded by name) and checks existence only, never status, against .beads/issues.jsonl. Run against the full corpus: 377 citations across 44 files, 0 missing — no rot found, nothing to fix. A missing tracker export fails loudly rather than passing on an empty id set. Exempted by name in lint-no-bead-refs.mjs's excluded list alongside reconcile-tracker/repo-gate/labeling-kit, since its own scan and its test fixtures hold bead ids as data, not lineage.

3. scripts/lint-skill-pack-skew.mjs (new): reuses projectSkillsPack and skillPackSkew from src/kernel/skills/projection.ts (imported, not reimplemented) to compare the committed .claude/skills/construct-* pack against what LENSES + allPlaybooks() + LENS_STANDARDS would generate right now, byte for byte. skillPackSkew alone only catches a stamped-version mismatch (comparing the frontmatter version field against packageVersion()); it cannot see the ordinary drift case — lenses.ts edited, not yet regenerated, package.json version unchanged — so the byte comparison against a freshly projected pack is the check that actually gates. Only folders carrying the `generator: construct` marker (isGeneratedSkill) are judged, so a hand-authored skill coexisting in the directory is never flagged. Re-checked repeatedly through the session against a moving HEAD, since another session was regenerating the pack from lenses.ts in parallel (their landing commit, dc3f8c67, had already merged before this session started): clean every time it was checked, 15/15 folders matched. No skew found; nothing to report as unresolved.

4. Docs staleness sweep (docs/*.md, skip generated org-map.md and dated docs/skill-runs/): six clear fixes applied — "currently" dropped from a print-behavior claim in 2026-08-21-shape-chooser-miss-rate.md; "checked manually today" in prd-agentic-platform.md dated to the day it actually happened (2026-08-21); two bare `kernel/...` paths in injected-ground-review.md and persona-acceptance-rubrics.md given the missing src/ prefix every other kernel-path citation in the corpus already uses; prd-agentic-platform.md's Open questions section rewritten from "reports 2 open questions as of this PRD's authoring... both have since been answered and shipped" to stating the settled facts directly, without the stacked-amendment framing. Judgment call, left alone rather than guessed: the word "now" recurs roughly 30 times across the docs corpus but on inspection is overwhelmingly legitimate — contrastive change narrative, one quoted external page title ("...is now GA"), and settled-decision-log entries inside stakeholder-acceptance-phase-4.md/phase-5.md that a prior session already swept for this exact concern (construct-4rcs, "A phase states what is true once, not five amendments a reader has to replay"). Reviewed case by case; none of the "now" instances met the bar for a mechanical fix, so none were touched.

Gate: full chain run as one command, `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke`, exit 0. 2770/2770 tests passed (no sharding needed; completed in ~19s with no OOM). Re-ran clean a second time after the commit landed.
2026-08-21 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): branch lag. Landing commit(s) 6815a4ff on claude/construct-vision-direction-sn3qg5, not yet merged to main, so a grep of main finds nothing. Re-reports until the branch merges.

title: The pre-commit hook stages a whole-database tracker export into whatever commit is running
description:
Gerald, 2026-08-21: 'this seems like an anti pattern'. It is.

The active pre-commit hook (.beads/hooks/pre-commit, reached through core.hooksPath) chains two managed sections. The beads section runs 'bd hooks run pre-commit', which re-exports the entire tracker database to .beads/issues.jsonl and stages it. The export is whole-database, so it carries every bead any session touched, and the staging attaches that to whatever commit happens to be in flight.

Reproduced tonight rather than theorized: commit 212f9773, whose author staged exactly two files by name, carries an issues.jsonl diff holding five unrelated beads (construct-wwun, construct-dr48, construct-wwun.1, construct-chno.3, construct-fdl) written concurrently by a different session. The work is real and correctly recorded; it is attributed to the wrong commit.

Two things are wrong, and the second holds even with one session:

1. Concurrent sessions have their tracker writes swept into each other's commits, so git history misattributes who recorded what.
2. This repository's own convention is one commit per bead whose first line states the invariant that commit establishes. A commit whose diff also carries unrelated bead JSON contradicts that, single-session or not.

Nothing depends on the staging. bd's auto-export (export.auto, default true) already rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl after every write command, so the file on disk stays fresh without any commit, and that on-disk file is what src/hosts/repo/evidence.ts (EXPORT_PATH) reads for npm run reconcile. Only the git add is load-bearing for nothing.

The commit shape is not observed uniformly, which is why this went unnoticed: during a pathspec commit (git commit -- path) git holds the index and the hook's git add fails harmlessly, so those commits are clean. An index-based commit (git add then git commit) picks the export up.
design:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A commit whose author did not stage .beads/issues.jsonl does not carry it, whether the commit was made with a pathspec or from the index.
- A commit whose author DID stage it still carries it, with the freshest export rather than a stale one, so a deliberate tracker-state commit keeps working.
- The export itself is untouched: .beads/issues.jsonl on disk still refreshes on every bd write, and npm run reconcile still reads current state.
- The beads-managed section of the hook is not edited. It carries its own markers and a bd upgrade rewrites it.
- A test exercises both directions against a real scratch repository, not a mock.
- npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke.
notes:
2026-08-21 FIXED, landed f7447e09. The keeper section runs last in .beads/hooks/pre-commit, after the beads-managed section it undoes, and takes .beads/issues.jsonl back out of the index. The gate section runs first and is the only place that can observe whether the author staged it, so it records that answer under the git dir for the keeper to read. The beads block is untouched, markers and all.

Proved on the fix's own landing rather than only in a test: that commit's hook re-exported 435 issues and the commit carries four files, none of them the export.

Test is tests/scripts/install-git-hooks.test.ts, against a real scratch git repository with the beads section stubbed by a block that stages the export unconditionally, which is the one behavior that matters. Five cases: section ordering with the beads markers intact, a commit the author did not stage it into, one the author did, a pathspec commit, and re-running the installer twice with a behavioral check after.

Gate green on a clean checkout of f7447e09 in a scratch worktree, not on the shared tree: lint clean, typecheck clean, 2751 tests pass across three shards, smoke pass.

Companion change in CLAUDE.md: session close now commits the export deliberately as its own commit. Removing the automatic mechanism means naming the deliberate one. Tracker state does not live in that file and cannot be lost by skipping it, but the reconcile's second witness reads the file's git history for closes the database lost, and that history needs revisions to read.
2026-08-21 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): branch lag. Landing commit f7447e09 is on claude/construct-vision-direction-sn3qg5, which is not yet merged to main, so a grep of main finds nothing. Re-reports until the branch merges.
close_reason: Closed

title: Codex exec reports MCP tool calls as user-cancelled even when they complete and mutate state
description:
## Summary

Attaching construct serve to codex-cli 0.145.0 as an MCP server (via `codex exec -c mcp_servers.construct.command=... -c mcp_servers.construct.args=...`, or loading it from a real config.toml entry) and asking the model to call a tool produces `{"error":{"message":"user cancelled MCP tool call"}}` on every call, reported to the model as a failure. But the underlying JSON-RPC call is not actually blocked: construct serve receives it, processes it, and (for record_outcome) writes a real run into the store — the model is told the action failed when it actually succeeded.

## Steps to Reproduce

From /Users/geralddagher/Developer/Projects/construct (a directory already `trust_level = "trusted"` in ~/.codex/config.toml, ruling out workspace trust as the cause):

```
codex exec --json --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check -s read-only \
  -c mcp_servers.construct.command=node \
  -c 'mcp_servers.construct.args=["/Users/geralddagher/Developer/Projects/construct/bin/construct.mjs","serve"]' \
  'Call the construct MCP tool named record_outcome with outcome set to exactly: "..."' < /dev/null
```

Event stream: `item.completed` for the `record_outcome` call shows `"error":{"message":"user cancelled MCP tool call"},"status":"failed"`, and the model's final reply reports the tool call as having failed.

Cross-checked independently against the real store (`node bin/construct.mjs log`): a new work-log entry `outcome-received` / `implication-named (inferred by: cache)` appears at the exact timestamp the codex turn completed, for the exact outcome text submitted — the run was recorded despite codex telling the model it was cancelled. A raw timing probe (`echo '...' | node bin/construct.mjs serve`, wrapped in `time`) shows construct serve answers a real call in ~0.1s, ruling out a startup-timeout explanation.

Control, same invocation shape, same session: a tool call to `sequential-thinking` (already present in the real ~/.codex/config.toml, no auth required) completes normally with a real result relayed to the model — no cancellation. The cancellation reproduced identically whether the directory was trusted or untrusted, and whether `--ignore-user-config` was used or not, so directory/workspace trust is not the variable; the best-supported distinction from this session's evidence is "declared via `-c mcp_servers.*` CLI overrides" vs. "already present as a real config.toml entry," but that was not conclusively isolated — doing so would require running `codex mcp add construct -- ...` against a real config.toml, which this trial deliberately did not do without separate approval (see docs/host-trial-codex.md).

## Why this matters

docs/host-interaction.md lists "Codex MCP" as one of the places construct's projection already attaches. A false cancellation is worse than an honest block (contrast: cursor-agent's headless `-p` mode cleanly rejects the same kind of call with no side effect at all — see docs/host-trial-cursor.md). Anyone scripting or dispatching against construct's projection through codex has no reliable signal from the tool-call result alone that a write actually landed, and a caller that retries a call it wrongly believes failed will create additional real runs and queue additional real tasks, silently.

## Suggested Direction

Not prescriptive, and nothing to fix in this repository's own code — construct serve already answers correctly and fast; the mismatch is entirely inside codex's own client harness, after it has the correct reply and before it reaches the model. The concrete, owned fix is documentation: docs/host-interaction.md's Codex MCP mention should name this hazard, and recommend that anyone attaching construct to codex do so via `codex mcp add` (a real, persisted registration — confirmed by this trial's `sequential-thinking` control to behave differently from an ad-hoc `-c` override) and independently verify a write landed via the CLI rather than trusting the tool-call result codex relays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- docs/host-interaction.md's Codex MCP entry states plainly that a codex-relayed tool-call failure is not reliable evidence the call did not happen, with a pointer to verifying via the CLI.
- Whether `codex mcp add` (persisted registration) avoids the false-cancellation is verified against a live binary rather than left as this trial's untested inference, without writing to any real, in-use ~/.codex/config.toml except with the account owner's own explicit action.
- Full repo gate green (npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke).
notes: 2026-08-21 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): retracted the same session it was filed, on a disproven premise (see the close reason). No code in this repository needed to change, so there is no landing commit to point to and none is expected; the corrected finding is recorded in docs/host-trial-codex.md instead, landed on main-bound commit 6b76790c (construct-chno.3).
close_reason: Retracted: filed on an incomplete verification. The original repro (this session, 2026-08-21) showed codex reporting "user cancelled MCP tool call" for a record_outcome call, then found a matching work-log entry at nearly the same timestamp and concluded the call had actually landed despite the reported cancellation. A follow-up test in the same session, using a unique, never-before-seen outcome text ("zzz-codex-cancel-probe-9f3e1c4a2b...") specifically so any store mutation would be unambiguously attributable, disproves that: the probe text never appears in the work log after the same "user cancelled" response. The two log entries that looked like corroboration were a coincidence of a shared, concurrently-written store and a reused real outcome sentence (the same BlackStory text construct-chno.4's goose trial used) — not evidence of this session's own calls landing. Corrected finding: codex's ad-hoc-MCP-server cancellation is an honest block (no phantom write), the same shape as cursor-agent's headless MCP rejection recorded in docs/host-trial-cursor.md, not a false-success mismatch. Recorded as an observation in docs/host-trial-codex.md rather than refiled as a bug, on the same reasoning docs/host-trial-cursor.md and the goose/pi trials already used: a host's own non-interactive approval gate, with normal interactive use unaffected and no Construct-side code to change.

title: record_outcome's description does not say identical outcome text overrides namings from a cache
description:
## Summary

record_outcome (src/hosts/mcp/projection.ts) is backed by a store-level naming cache keyed on the exact outcome string (src/kernel/store/namings.ts): 'the first answer stands, and a second consultation of the same outcome does not overwrite the reason the first one cited.' That is a deliberate, well-reasoned, documented design (do not change it without cause) for cost control and determinism. The gap is narrower: the record_outcome tool's own description, which is the only thing a calling host or model ever reads before calling it, never mentions this. It says only 'anything outside the catalog or without a reason is discarded by the kernel, and the reply says what was admitted' — read plainly, that is an exhaustive account of why a naming might not be admitted, and it is not: a third, unstated reason exists.

## Steps to Reproduce

Found in the goose trial for construct-chno.4 (docs/host-trial-goose.md), on goose's claude-code provider (Gerald's Claude Code subscription, claude-sonnet-5). An outcome text already consulted once (recorded earlier the same session under a different run) was submitted again with a fresh, well-reasoned five-domain namings proposal. Claude noticed on its own, from the raw tool reply, and said so unprompted: 'the kernel's admitted result (inferredBy: "cache") did not take my namings as submitted... worth flagging if you expect namings to be authoritative, since here it wasn't.'

Reproduced directly against the server, independent of any host or model, with a minimal case: a single well-formed naming (domain 'coverage-gaps', a real catalog domain, with a valid why) against the same already-cached outcome text returns the OLD cached implicated set (five different domains from an earlier, unrelated consultation) and places the new, perfectly valid proposal in notAdmitted, with inferredBy:"cache" as the only signal anything unusual happened:

node bin/construct.mjs serve, piped tools/call for record_outcome with a fresh single naming against a previously-consulted outcome string, returns:
{"run":"...","implicated":[...five domains from the FIRST consultation...],"inferredBy":"cache","tasksQueued":5,"notAdmitted":["coverage-gaps"]}

## Why this is a real gap, not just the cache working as designed

The signal is technically present (inferredBy:"cache" on the same reply notAdmitted names), so a caller who already knows to check it can figure out what happened, exactly as Claude did here by reasoning about the raw JSON. But nothing in the tool description tells a caller this can happen or that inferredBy is worth inspecting for this reason, and notAdmitted does not distinguish 'discarded, not in the catalog' from 'discarded, an earlier unrelated consultation already answered this exact text' — both land in the same array with no differentiated reason. A caller (host, script, or person) that trusts the description's stated exhaustive list of discard reasons has no way to anticipate a well-formed, catalog-valid, reasoned naming can still be silently overridden by whoever happened to submit the identical outcome text first, from an entirely different session or host.

## Suggested Direction

Not prescriptive: options include stating the cache behavior in record_outcome's own description, adding a distinguishing reason (not just presence/absence) to notAdmitted entries, or a dedicated field naming which proposals were shadowed by a cache hit versus rejected outright. Left as a bug rather than fixed in place because construct-chno.4's scope is the goose/pi trial packets, not a projection description change, and the right shape for the fix is a judgment call this description should not make unilaterally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- record_outcome's tool description states that an outcome text already consulted (by any host, in any prior session) returns the cached answer rather than consulting the caller's own namings.
- A caller has a way, from the reply alone, to distinguish a naming discarded for being outside the catalog or reasonless from one discarded because a cache hit served an unrelated earlier answer.
- Existing cache behavior and its cost/determinism rationale (src/kernel/store/namings.ts) are unchanged.
- Full repo gate green (npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke).
acceptance_criteria: record_outcome's description states the cache-override behavior; a caller can distinguish a catalog/reasonless rejection from a cache-shadowed one in the reply; cache semantics themselves are unchanged; full repo gate green.
notes:
2026-08-21 Fixed: record_outcome's tool description now states the cache-override behavior plainly — an outcome text already consulted once (by any host, any prior session) is served from a store-level cache, the fresh namings are not evaluated against the catalog at all, and any proposed domain missing from the cached answer lands in notAdmitted. The projection's startedReply() now adds a notAdmittedBecause field when inferredBy is 'cache' and notAdmitted is non-empty, so a caller no longer has to infer a cache-shadowed rejection by cross-referencing inferredBy on its own; a genuine catalog/reasonless rejection carries no such field. kernel/store/namings.ts's cache behavior itself is unchanged, as required. Tests added: tests/hosts/mcp/projection.test.ts (cache-hit case, non-cache-hit case, tool-description assertion). Landing commit: 117401cc.
2026-08-21 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): branch lag. Landing commit 117401cc is on claude/construct-vision-direction-sn3qg5, which is not yet merged to main, so a grep of main finds nothing. Re-reports until the branch merges.
close_reason: record_outcome's description now states the cache-override behavior, and notAdmittedBecause distinguishes a cache-shadowed rejection from a catalog/reasonless one; cache behavior itself unchanged; tests added; full gate green.

title: Development scripts still default to a local model server, against the standing sourcing rule
description:
Gerald's 2026-08-21 directive (now in CLAUDE.md's conventions): every model call made to build or verify this repository comes from Claude Code or Cursor, never from Ollama or another local server. Several development scripts still default the other way, so a session that omits a flag silently violates the rule.

Verified by grep 2026-08-21: scripts/measure-decisions.mjs:814 defaults NAMER_HOST to 'ollama' and :817 defaults its model to qwen3.5:4b when the host is ollama; scripts/probe-goose-conformance.mjs:29 and scripts/probe-pi-conformance.mjs:34 default the provider to 'ollama' when the model argument carries no provider prefix; scripts/probe-pi-conformance.mjs:176 hard-codes an ollama provider in one check; scripts/probe-ground-routing.mjs:190 branches on an 'ollama' transport.

The correct replacement default is per host and is not uniform. goose reaches Claude Code through its own claude-code provider. codex and cursor-agent carry their vendor subscriptions directly. opencode and pi may have no subscription-backed path at all from an autonomous session, in which case the honest outcome is that the probe records the gap rather than falling back to a local model, per the same rule.
design:
## Acceptance Criteria

- No development script defaults to a local model server. Every default names a subscription-backed path, or the script refuses and says what to pass rather than choosing one.
- The per-host answer is recorded, not assumed: for each of claude, cursor, codex, goose, opencode and pi, the script says which subscription-backed model it reaches, or states that none is reachable and refuses.
- A probe target with no subscription-backed path records that as a gap in its pin or packet. It never silently falls back to a local model.
- npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke.
notes:
2026-08-21 Filed on Gerald's directive, in the same session that recorded it in CLAUDE.md. Blocked in practice on the two host-trial beads in flight (construct-chno.3 for codex/opencode/cursor, construct-chno.4 for goose/pi): those trials are what establish which subscription-backed model each host can actually reach, and guessing a default before they report would put the same assumption back in a different place.

2026-08-21 DISPATCH — Sonnet-class or better, self-contained once the two trial beads report. Mechanical once the per-host answer exists: flip each default, and make any host with no subscription-backed path refuse with a message naming what to pass instead of choosing for the caller. Do NOT delete the ollama code paths: this rule governs development sourcing, not the product's support for a user who chooses a local model, and those are different things. Close gate: the full repo gate.
2026-08-21 UNBLOCKED: both trial beads closed, and they answer the per-host question this was waiting on. What each host can actually reach, from the recorded packets:
- goose: reaches Claude Code through its own claude-code provider (docs/host-trial-goose.md, run on --provider claude-code --model claude-sonnet-5). This is the replacement default.
- codex: ChatGPT subscription, works (docs/host-trial-codex.md). Note the trial found codex refuses a headless MCP call registered ad hoc, which is host-owned behavior and not a Construct defect.
- cursor-agent: Cursor subscription, works (docs/host-trial-cursor.md), with headless calls gated by cursor's own approvalMode allowlist.
- opencode: NO subscription-backed path. Stored credentials for GitHub Copilot and OpenCode Go expose zero invocable model IDs, confirmed by a direct failing call. Its probe should refuse and name what to pass rather than defaulting to anything.
- pi: no MCP client at all, and its Claude Pro/Max login is interactive-only with no non-interactive equivalent. Same treatment as opencode.
The two hosts with no path are the case the acceptance criteria already cover: refuse and say what to pass, never fall back to something local.
2026-08-21 IMPLEMENTED, gate green, closing. Per-host defaults flipped: measure-decisions.mjs's --namer arm (NAMER_HOST) and probe-goose-conformance.mjs (--model) now default to claude and claude-code/claude-sonnet-5 respectively, in place of ollama; both still reach ollama on an explicit --namer-host ollama / --model ollama/<model>. probe-opencode-conformance.mjs, capture-opencode-transcripts.mjs, and probe-pi-conformance.mjs now refuse (exit 2, message naming what to pass) when no explicit model is given, since opencode and pi have no subscription-backed path at all - verified live, each prints its refusal and exits 2 with no flags. probe-pi-conformance.mjs also stopped hardcoding 'ollama' as the throwaway provider name in its zero-providers-configured negative check (replaced with a synthetic name, since that check never reaches a real model and the literal was only ever a red herring for a sourcing grep). probe-ground-routing.mjs needed no behavior change: its --namer arm was already always-explicit with no default at all (a bare --namer=<transport>/<model> is mandatory to use it, and omitting --namer entirely skips the model call), so only a clarifying comment was added. CLAUDE.md's probe:opencode line updated to require --tool-model too, matching the new refusal.

Verified, not just read: ran the real refusal paths for pi and opencode live (exit 2, correct message each time) and ran the goose probe live end to end against its new claude-code default (goose 1.46.0, claude-code/claude-sonnet-5) - 6 of 8 pinned expectations pass; the 2 that fail were measured only against ollama to begin with (pin.ts's own header says so) and do not hold under claude-code, filed as construct-smgc rather than patched here since fixing pin.ts's claims needs its own look.

Added a test proving the measure-decisions.mjs default is load-bearing (tests/scripts/measure-decisions-attribution.test.ts: omitting --namer-host now reaches the claude-host refusal instead of silently dialling ollama).

Gate: npm run lint clean, npm run typecheck clean, npm test 2752/2752 pass (no sharding needed), npm run smoke pass. Commit 8f7c9896, touching exactly CLAUDE.md, scripts/measure-decisions.mjs, scripts/probe-goose-conformance.mjs, scripts/probe-pi-conformance.mjs, scripts/probe-opencode-conformance.mjs, scripts/capture-opencode-transcripts.mjs, scripts/probe-ground-routing.mjs, tests/scripts/measure-decisions-attribution.test.ts.

Out of scope, deliberately left untouched: scripts/run-org-harness-ollama.mjs (a dedicated, explicitly-named ollama harness variant, not a silent default), scripts/measure-panel-agreement.mjs and scripts/labeling-kit/code-sheet-with-model.mjs (deliberate cross-family independent-coder tooling under the LLM-as-judge convention, where a non-Anthropic-family local model is the point, not a cost shortcut), scripts/probe-model-contract.mjs (already refuses without an explicit --model), measure-decisions.mjs's --embeddings section (hardcoded to nomic-embed-text, gated behind its own flag, no subscription-backed embeddings alternative exists to default to instead). CHANGELOG.md's 3.0.0-alpha.0 entry describing the old ollama-default behavior is left as the dated historical record it is, not rewritten.
2026-08-21 DRIFT ADJUDICATED (closed-without-commit): branch lag. Landing commit(s) 8f7c9896 on claude/construct-vision-direction-sn3qg5, not yet merged to main, so a grep of main finds nothing. Re-reports until the branch merges.
close_reason: Six scripts (measure-decisions.mjs, probe-goose/-pi/-opencode-conformance.mjs, capture-opencode-transcripts.mjs, probe-ground-routing.mjs) plus CLAUDE.md's documented invocation now match the sourcing rule: subscription-backed defaults where one exists (claude / claude-code), a named refusal where none does (opencode, pi). Ollama stays reachable on an explicit ask. Gate green, commit 8f7c9896. Full account in NOTES.

title: construct log --run=<id> silently ignores the flag and dumps the whole log instead of erroring
description:
## Summary

src/cli/show.ts's log() (line 185) parses --run with only 'const runIndex = argv.indexOf(--run); const run = runIndex >= 0 ? argv[runIndex + 1] : undefined;' (line 186-187) — argv.indexOf only matches the exact token --run, so --run=<id> (one argv token, no space) is never found and run stays undefined, silently falling through to the unscoped whole-log branch. No error, no warning.

## Steps to Reproduce

Found verifying construct-chno.4's goose trial from the standalone CLI (docs/host-trial-goose.md), the same way host-trial-nanobot.md verified its recorded runs from the CLI.

1. node bin/construct.mjs log --run=run-20260821212338703  (equals form)
   -> prints the entire unscoped log: 1092 lines, going back to 2026-08-04, no error.
2. node bin/construct.mjs log --run run-20260821212338703  (space form)
   -> correctly prints that run's 7 scoped entries plus the task-state footer.

## Why this is a real outlier, not a project-wide gap

show() in the SAME FILE (line 104-106) already handles both forms: "argv.find((a) => a.startsWith('--run='))...  ?? (runIndex >= 0 ? ...)". src/cli/work.ts's parseWorkArgs and src/cli/verdict.ts's parseVerdictArgs both handle both forms too — verdict.ts's own comment explains why: 'log and work both take the spaced form and a user who learned it there types it here. This surface refusing it sent people to a usage error at the one step the routing corpus depends on' — i.e. this exact inconsistency was already hit once for verdict and worked around there rather than fixed at the source. log's own sibling show() in the same file is further evidence the equals form is this surface's own norm, not an unsupported syntax choice.

## Compounds with construct-chno.5

work_log/log have no size bound when unscoped (construct-chno.5). A user or script that mistypes --run=<id> on log does not get an error — they get well over a thousand lines standing in for the seven they asked for, shaped just like a correct answer only longer, with nothing marking it as the wrong scope.

## Suggested Direction

Not prescriptive: make log's --run parsing accept --run=<id> the same way its own show() sibling and work/verdict already do, or adopt src/cli/flags.ts's splitFlags/parseFlags so every verb agrees (that module's stated purpose: 'One place, because the surfaces have to agree'). Separately worth deciding: whether an unrecognized/malformed flag on a scoping argument should error rather than silently no-op into the unscoped path — left to whoever picks this up. Not fixed in place because construct-chno.4's scope is the goose/pi trial packets, not a CLI parsing change, and src/cli/work.ts is off-limits in this session (concurrent edit in progress).

## Acceptance Criteria

- construct log --run=<id> scopes the same as construct log --run <id>.
- A test asserts both forms produce identical output for the same run.
- Full repo gate green (npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke).
acceptance_criteria: construct log --run=<id> and construct log --run <id> produce identical, correctly-scoped output; a test asserts this; full repo gate green.

title: MCP work_log tool returns the whole unscoped log with no limit, breaking host context budgets
description:
## Summary

construct serve's work_log MCP tool (src/hosts/mcp/projection.ts, tool declared ~line 151, handled at 'case work_log': return toolResult(id, { entries: readWorkLog(core.store, run) })) takes run as an optional scope. Omitting run falls through to src/kernel/store/worklog.ts's readWorkLog, whose own doc comment says 'Omit run to read the whole log' with a plain 'SELECT * FROM work_log ORDER BY seq' and no LIMIT. On a real, mature dogfood store this is well over a megabyte — impractical for any model's context budget, and the tool's own description ('Optionally scoped to one run') gives no hint of that.

## Steps to Reproduce

Found in the goose trial for construct-chno.4 (docs/host-trial-goose.md). A real run through goose (local Ollama qwen3.5:4b, --with-extension attaching 'node bin/construct.mjs serve') recorded a real outcome, then on its own initiative called work_log with no run argument. goose could not inline the reply: 'The response returned from the tool call was larger (1326114 characters) and is stored in the file...' — it spooled the result to a temp file instead of returning it to the model.

Reproduced directly against the MCP server, independent of goose: piping a tools/call for work_log with no arguments into 'node bin/construct.mjs serve' returns a 1,385,133-byte JSON-RPC response on this machine's real store. For comparison, on the same store: run_status unscoped is 23,091 bytes, asks unscoped is 7,409 bytes, inbox is 17,683 bytes — all bounded by what is currently open or active. work_log is the outlier because it is the literal, ever-growing append-only table with no cap.

## Why this is not the same as the CLI's construct log

src/cli/show.ts's log command reads the same unscoped rows and has the same lack of a bound, but a human at a terminal can scroll, pipe to less/grep, or stop reading. A model behind the MCP tool has a hard context budget and no equivalent agency, so the identical default that is reasonable on the CLI is a practical break over MCP specifically.

## Suggested Direction

Not prescriptive: options include requiring run for this MCP surface specifically, applying a default max-entries limit with a stated truncation note, or another bound chosen by whoever owns src/hosts/mcp/projection.ts. Left as a bug rather than fixed in place because construct-chno.4's scope is the goose/pi trial packets, not a projection behavior change, and the right bound is a judgment call this bead should not make unilaterally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An unscoped work_log MCP call against a real, mature store returns a bounded reply (by count, size, or a required run) instead of the entire table.
- If truncated or refused, the reply states that plainly so a caller does not mistake a partial or empty result for the whole log.
- Existing behavior of run-scoped work_log calls is unchanged.
- The CLI's construct log (human-consumed, scrollable) is explicitly considered and left alone unless the fix naturally covers both — this bead is about the MCP tool's caller, not the terminal's.
- Full repo gate green (npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke).
acceptance_criteria: An unscoped work_log MCP call against a real, mature store returns a bounded reply (by count, size, or a required run) instead of the entire table; a truncated/refused reply states so plainly; run-scoped calls are unchanged; full repo gate green.
notes:
2026-08-21 Fixed: work_log's run argument is now required at the MCP tool level (inputSchema required: ['run'], plus a handler-level RangeError naming what to pass when omitted). Unlike run_status/asks/inbox, work_log has no natural bound — those three stay small because they reflect only current state, not the whole append-only history — so its previously-optional-looking schema was the real outlier. The fix reuses the codebase's existing 'required field, no reasonable default, refuse and name it' convention already used by records/record/answer/decide/verdict in the same file, rather than inventing a new truncation mechanism. Run-scoped calls are unchanged. Test added: tests/hosts/mcp/projection.test.ts ('work_log refuses an unscoped call...'). Landing commit: 117401cc.

title: No brief the planner writes ever declares a modelFloor, so every floor check compares against 'any'
description:
Verified by grep 2026-08-21: modelFloor appears in src/kernel/brief/schema.ts (declared, validated), src/kernel/brief/satisfy.ts and src/kernel/run/coordinator.ts (both read it and degrade when unmet), and nowhere else. Every brief the planner builds sets capabilities: [] and no modelFloor (src/kernel/run/outcome.ts briefFor). So the degradation path, the satisfy resolution, and the new resource selection in src/kernel/hosts/selection.ts all compute against a floor of 'any' on every real run, and the clears/degraded distinction can only fire on a hand-written brief.

Either the planner should declare a floor per domain (judgment-heavy lenses need frontier; mechanical ones do not), or the field should be documented as caller-supplied only. Today it reads as a live requirement and is dead in practice.
acceptance_criteria: Either every planner-built brief declares a modelFloor appropriate to its domain (and a test proves a judgment-heavy domain declares above 'any'), or schema.ts documents the field as caller-supplied and the surfaces that read it say so. npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run smoke.

The selector reads the strongest modelFloor across a run's pending briefs; with no planner ever setting one, it always reads 'any', so the degraded rung is currently reachable only from a hand-written brief. Filed rather than fixed: changing what floors the planner declares is a policy call about the lens catalog, not part of the selection mechanism.
