title: Audit low-severity cluster: skills-install overwrite/TOCTOU, backup mode window, unpinned npx, connector-gate lint blindspot, stale lockfile version
description:
Six low findings from the 2026-08 audit, each small and independent:
- L13 skills install (cli/skills.ts:345-358) silently overwrites a user-edited SKILL.md; library.ts:160-168 can already detect diverged but install never consults it. Fix: refuse a diverged target unless --force; test.
- L14 TOCTOU between the skills symlink guard (skills.ts:333-342) and the write (:345-358); writeFileSync follows a symlink at the final component. Fix: openSync wx/w with O_NOFOLLOW or temp-then-rename. Low (needs write access to target dir) but the guard comment claims a stronger property than delivered.
- L15 backup file world-readable between VACUUM INTO and chmod (backup.ts:157-165) — seconds-to-minutes window with a complete readable copy. Fix: pre-create openSync(file,wx,0600) or stage in mkdtemp then rename.
- L16 README:19, skills/README.md:39 (ships in tarball), and skills.ts:136 (printed as remediation) hand the user 'npx skills add geraldmaron/construct' — Vercel's installer, a package this project does not control, at floating latest, writing into ~/.claude/skills — offered as interchangeable with running our own CLI. Fix: name the third-party boundary or pin npx skills@<version>.
- L17 lint-connector-gate.mjs:66-67 matches only string-literal import specifiers; a computed import(base+name) or createRequire is invisible. Fix: fail the lint on any import( whose argument is not a string literal.
- L18 package-lock.json:3 says 3.0.0-alpha.15, package.json:3 says alpha.16; npm ci still succeeds and release.yml verifies the tag against package.json only. Fix: sync the lockfile; a check that lock root version matches package.json.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Full repo gate passes.

title: Opt-in repo-local state, refused unless the store path is ignored
description:
For the fully-embedded case (contractor laptop, disposable environment): a ratified project file may declare state: local, rooting the sqlite store under .construct/state/ instead of the home directory. Doctor and every store-opening path refuse to run repo-local unless the path is covered by the repo's ignore rules — a store of client facts must never be committable by accident. Lowest-priority piece of the settings program: ratified workspace binding already gives most of the isolation with none of the risk. Blocked by the project-declaration bead.

title: Divergence sweeps rebuild each watch's whole firing history every time
description:
lastObservedChange walks the entire unbounded firing history of the far watch and rebuilds document-diff maps across every consecutive pair on every 'watch --due' sweep, per edge touching a moved source: O(edges x history x documents), recomputed from scratch, so sweeps slow as a watch ages rather than as work grows. Bound or incrementalize it: read history newest-first with a limit sufficient to find the last change, or record the last-change summary at firing time so the sweep reads one row. Measured gate before close: a synthetic long-history fixture demonstrating the sweep no longer scales with total history length.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'watch --due' cost per edge no longer grows with total firing history (test over a long-history fixture asserting bounded reads or comparing query counts).
- Divergence findings unchanged on the existing watch tests.
- Full repo gate passes.

title: A divergence watch over a relation with an unwatched far end is silently inert
description:
edgeDivergenceFindings deliberately raises nothing when the relation's other end has no active watch (correct anti-false-positive design), but nothing tells the user: the realistic default (watch your repo, not the strategy doc it depends on) leaves the promised divergence consumer dark forever with no diagnostic. Add the missing surface: 'source relations' and/or 'watch --due' names relations whose divergence check is inert because one end is unwatched, and 'watch add' hints when a new watch completes or fails to complete a watched pair.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A relation with exactly one watched end is reported as divergence-inert on at least one read surface, naming the unwatched end.
- 'watch add' on a source with relations states which relations the new watch just made checkable, or that none changed.
- No behavior change to when findings fire; full repo gate passes.

title: Declaring supersedes silently blanks the old source from a whole run; the CLI never says so
description:
Intentional partitioning semantics (a superseded source does not travel with its superseder) surprise the user who declares one edge: the old source can vanish from every dispatch's ground with no warning at relate time and no line in 'source relations' saying the withholding is in force. Add a plain-language notice when a supersedes edge is declared, and have 'source relations' state what each relation currently does to ground assembly. Raised by an adversarial review of the relationship-graph change; the semantics stay, the silence goes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- 'construct source relate --relation=supersedes' prints one sentence stating the replaced source will be withheld from dispatches carrying its replacement.
- 'construct source relations' output states the ground-assembly effect of each active relation in plain language.
- Full repo gate passes.

title: docs/ and docs/internal/ can drift back together with nothing to stop them
description:
The 2026-08-22 split put user documentation in docs/ and development records in docs/internal/, but nothing enforces the boundary. A future session filing a dated probe transcript or an acceptance packet directly into docs/ would recreate exactly the mixture the split removed, and no gate would notice.

The distinction is a judgment rather than a pattern, which is why this is not obviously lintable: 'first-run.md' and 'host-trial-goose.md' differ by what they are for, not by anything in their names. A date-stamped filename is a strong signal and would catch several of the cases, but it would not catch org-coverage-plan.md or session-artifact-form.md, both of which are internal and undated.
acceptance_criteria: Either a check names a new docs/ file that looks like a development record and says so, or a dated recorded decision states that the boundary is maintained by review rather than by a gate, with the reason. Either way docs/internal/README.md states which it is.
close_reason: Resolved by making docs/ a closed set rather than by guessing at content. scripts/lint-docs-index.mjs holds docs/ and docs/README.md to each other in both directions and is in the lint chain; a new file fails until someone lists it as documentation or moves it to docs/internal/. The content heuristic the bead doubted was measured first and is recorded as rejected-with-reason in docs/internal/README.md: 13 of 16 records caught, three missed, one false positive on a real guide — and false positives are the expensive kind. The marks survive as a printed hint, never a verdict. The one flagged file (host-interaction.md) was flagged correctly and moved. Lint exercised against all three failure modes before wiring. Full gate green, 2700 tests. Landed 2026-08-22.

title: A composed document does not tell its reader it was written outside the house voice
description:
Found while landing the compose voice override (2026-08-22). Both 'construct work --voice' and 'construct compose' now print the override to the operator's stdout, and the work log holds it as a durable record, but nothing stamps the composed document itself. A reader handed the markdown cannot tell it was written under a voice other than Construct's own.

This is consistent with how work has always behaved, which is why it was not changed inside the override bead — but it is a disclosure gap of exactly the kind this repository normally closes, and whether a deliverable discloses its own voice is a separate decision from whether the voice reaches the deliverable at all.
acceptance_criteria: Either a composed document carries a visible statement of the voice it was written under, or a dated recorded decision says a deliverable deliberately does not disclose its voice and why; either way a test pins the chosen behavior.

title: goose's claude-code provider does not match two ollama-measured expectations in its pin
description:
src/hosts/goose/pin.ts's EXPECTATIONS were measured only against goose's ollama provider (its own header comment says so: 'against a local Ollama backend'). construct-iqpw just made claude-code the default provider scripts/probe-goose-conformance.mjs runs against, since that is goose's subscription-backed path per CLAUDE.md's sourcing rule. Running the probe for real against claude-code (goose 1.46.0, claude-code/claude-sonnet-5, 2026-08-21) surfaced two of the eight pinned expectations failing:

1. a-failed-model-call-exits-0-and-reads-as-success — the pin's claim is specifically 'measured: an unrecognised model name against Ollama, a 404'. Against claude-code, requesting the deliberately-bogus model 'construct-probe-nonexistent-model' did NOT produce the documented error text; goose replied normally with 'pong', exit 0, status completed. The claude-code provider (shelling out to the local claude CLI) appears not to validate --model the way ollama's tag lookup does.
2. no-session-skips-the-shared-session-store-but-not-the-request-log — the request-log freshness check (~/.local/state/goose/logs/llm_request.*.jsonl mtime) showed before == after across every call in the run. claude-code's shelled-out execution does not appear to write to goose's own request log the way its native HTTP-backed providers do.

Full run transcript (node scripts/probe-goose-conformance.mjs, no flags, new default):
6 of 8 pass (version-flag-reports-the-version, run-accepts-a-prompt-non-interactively, quiet-is-required-for-clean-stdout-in-every-format, output-format-json-is-one-object-not-ndjson, usage-is-token-counts-only-no-cost-field, explicit-provider-and-model-flags-override-a-configured-default). The 2 above FAIL.

Neither looks like a probe bug: the check code is untouched by construct-iqpw, and both readings are internally consistent (a real reply reached stdout in case 1; a real mtime was read twice in case 2). This reads as true per-provider behavior the pin's claims do not yet scope — pin.ts's own file comment already models exactly this shape for a different host (probe-pi-conformance.mjs's failed-turn-exit-signal-depends-on-mode expectation states two mode-dependent behaviors explicitly instead of one averaged claim); goose's pin likely needs the same per-provider treatment for these two, or an explicit note that they are unprobed/undefined outside ollama.

Not fixed here: determining whether this is a claim-wording gap (most likely) or an actual goose defect needs its own look, and constructing-iqpw's scope is sourcing defaults, not a pin audit.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) pin.ts's two affected EXPECTATIONS are reworded to state what each provider actually does (mirroring probe-pi-conformance.mjs's mode-dependent pattern), and probe-goose-conformance.mjs's checks are updated to match per provider; or (b) the two expectations are explicitly marked unprobed-under-claude-code with a recorded reason, matching UNPROBED_EXPECTATIONS conventions elsewhere in this repo. Either way: node scripts/probe-goose-conformance.mjs (claude-code default) and node scripts/probe-goose-conformance.mjs --model ollama/qwen3.5:4b (explicit local) both documented as to their real, current pass/fail state, with no claim left stale.

title: The tracker export is not byte-stable, so the working tree never reads clean
description:
Exporting the tracker twice with no tracker change in between produces different bytes: the 8 memory records come out in a different order each time. Observed 2026-08-21 immediately after committing a fresh export, where 'git diff .beads/issues.jsonl' showed 4 insertions and 4 deletions, all of them memory lines moving, with no issue content changed.

Consequence: .beads/issues.jsonl is permanently dirty in every checkout, so 'git status' always shows a modification that means nothing. That is noise in its own right, and it also hides the case that matters, which is the export genuinely differing because tracker state moved. A derived file that never compares equal to itself cannot be used to tell whether anything changed.

This is bd's own export ordering, not something this repository controls, so the fix is either a deterministic sort applied on our side before the file is written, or an upstream report. Neither is urgent: the file's content is correct and the reconcile reads it fine.

title: A documented subcommand nobody can run still passes the doc-command lint
description:
scripts/lint-doc-commands.mjs checks the verb after 'construct' against the exported VERBS table and stops there. 'construct lessons list' passes because 'lessons' is real, even though no 'list' subcommand exists — and that exact line shipped in docs/first-run.md, which is the defect that motivated the lint.

Covering subcommands needs each verb to declare its own surface somewhere a check can read. Today subcommands are parsed inline per verb (see src/cli/source.ts, record.ts, staff.ts, standing.ts, watch.ts, propose.ts, skills.ts), so there is nothing central to compare against. Flags have the same shape of problem.

The narrow version is worth having on its own: it caught an invented verb, and the CHANGELOG records a shipped bug where the CLI told users to run 'construct install --with-docling', a predecessor command this CLI does not have.
design:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Each verb that takes subcommands declares them in a form a script can import, with the verb's own parser reading the same declaration rather than a second copy.
- lint-doc-commands.mjs checks the subcommand where one is declared, and says so in its output.
- A doc line naming a real verb with an invented subcommand fails the lint; a proof of the failing case is recorded the way the undeclared-seat guard's is.
- npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test pass.

title: Two concerns render as 'unmapped seat', which reads as a generator failure rather than a finding
description:
scripts/generate-org-map.mjs SEATS (lines 40-56) holds 15 entries against 17 DOMAINS. evidence-provenance and coverage-gaps fall through to the 'unmapped seat' fallback, so docs/org-map.md renders '### unmapped seat — evidence-provenance' and the same for coverage-gaps.

The output is not wrong: both carry a full lens and required deliverable slots, and neither maps onto a conventional job title. That is a real and interesting fact — they are the concerns that fall between seats, which is precisely why nobody on a human team is assigned to notice them. README.md now states it that way.

The defect is that 'unmapped seat' reads as a placeholder a generator emitted when its table was incomplete, not as a deliberate statement. A reader cannot tell the difference between 'no seat owns this, by finding' and 'someone forgot to add the row'.

Decide whether the fallback label should state the fact instead, and whether the page header's '17 of 17 concerns carry a lens' needs a companion sentence distinguishing lens coverage from seat coverage. Naming is linted for glossary parity, so the label is a vocabulary decision, not a free-text one.
design:

- The org-map's treatment of evidence-provenance and coverage-gaps distinguishes a deliberate absence of seat from an incomplete lookup table.
- Any new term clears scripts/lint-glossary-parity.mjs.

close_reason: DECIDED: persist per run, not re-pass per command; no compose --voice flag exists. The override was already durable — the coordinator writes it to the append-only, kernel-owned work log the moment a user's voice shapes a dispatch — and only the reader was missing, so compose now reads it back the way the recorded host and model already are, rather than asking the user to retype a fact the run holds. title: The extraction ladder's remediation names 'construct install', a command that does not exist
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. construct install --with-docling
2. Observe: the CLI prints the top-level usage line and does nothing. 'install' is not in USAGE (src/cli/index.ts) and has no case in the command switch.

## What happens

src/kernel/extract/ladder.ts tells the user to run that command in three separate remediation paths (lines 144, 286, 307): the generic docling-unavailable message, the OCR path, and the office-document path. Every one of them is a dead end. A user who hits an unextractable PDF, a scanned image, or a .docx without mammoth is handed an instruction that silently does nothing.

## Why it matters

Remediation text is the one place a user is already stuck, and this project's rule is that a failure names the recourse. Naming a recourse that does not exist is worse than naming none: the user assumes they typed it wrong.

## What to decide

Either build 'construct install --with-docling', or rewrite the three strings to name what actually works today (installing docling directly, or setting DOCLING_SERVE_URL with CONSTRUCT_EXTRACTION_PRIVACY=remote-ok). The strings were ported from the predecessor along with the ladder; the predecessor had that command and this rewrite does not.
acceptance_criteria: Either 'construct install --with-docling' exists and is in USAGE, or no remediation string in src/kernel/extract/ladder.ts names a command this CLI does not implement. A test asserts that every command named in a remediation string is one the CLI dispatches.
notes: 2026-08-11: found while tracing how Construct ingests datasets. Verified by running the command against the installed 3.0.0-alpha.4: prints usage, exits without acting.
close_reason: Three dead remediation strings replaced with working recourse; guard test enforces no src/ string names an unimplemented subcommand

title: A denial flood is the system's own evidence of a role fighting its grants, and it is surfaced nowhere
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Dispatch a role whose host retries a denied capability call (a record-verdict-shaped call, or repeated submit_draft past the cap).
2. construct log --run <id>; construct doctor

## What happens

Denials accumulate as append-only work log entries per src/cli/roleserve.ts. Neither construct log's run-state footer nor construct doctor reports a count. An operator finds a denial flood only by opening the raw work log and knowing to look for repeated denial entries.

## Why it matters

The denial record was built as evidence that a role is fighting its grants. Evidence nobody is shown is evidence that does not do its job — the same argument that put the limits label on the deliverable body rather than leaving it in the log.

## What to fix

A denial count in writeRunState's footer, or a doctor check, so a run with repeated denials reads differently from a clean one — the way a live lease already does.
acceptance_criteria: A run carrying denials reads differently from one that carries none, on a surface an operator already opens; a test drives it

title: The model-primary namer is unusable on 4b-class local models: record the capability floor instead of discovering it per run
description:
Found during the stakeholder-acceptance runs (construct-9xq): construct outcome --host=opencode --model=ollama/qwen3.5:4b returned malformed JSON from the namer on a plain outcome ('We want to hire a contractor in Poland to help with support'), so the run fell back to the keyword map. Run run-20260806032817359. The designed behavior worked exactly as intended — the failure is stated on screen, a namer-failed entry is written with the reason, and the keyword map answers rather than the run dying — so this is not a defect in the fallback. It is a missing statement of where the primary path actually works.

The matrix already has the vocabulary for this: src/hosts/tuning.ts records which families the producer prompts are validated against and every dispatch on an untuned family writes model-untuned-best-effort. Naming has no equivalent, so a user on a small local model discovers per outcome that the primary namer cannot hold the output contract, and pays a model call each time to find out.

title: Review run coordination constants against queueing and timeout theory
description:
Serves commitment 1.

DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY=2, DEFAULT_LEASE_MS=15min, and a spend ceiling checked before dispatch. Lowest-value item in this epic and filed as such — included so the decision surface is covered, not because these constants are suspected wrong.

Concurrency is an M/M/c queue; with per-task service time and the domain-count distribution derivable from the corpora, the latency/cost frontier says whether 2 sits on it. The lease is a timeout against a service-time distribution where too short duplicates work and too long strands it, so the instrument is the hazard rate of task completion — the existing comment establishes only a correctness lower bound (must exceed OpenCode's 10-minute timeout), not a choice of value. The spend ceiling is a knapsack over which domains to dispatch when the budget binds; dispatching score-descending is optimal only if cost is uniform across domains, which is unverified.

title: Model the completion ladder as an absorbing Markov chain with defect escape
description:
Serves commitment 13 (adversarial challenge is a contract).

completion/states.ts defines 12 rungs and promotion.ts derives draft -> challenged -> final from verdicts. Nobody knows which rung is the throughput bottleneck, because no transition probabilities are measured. An absorbing Markov chain over the rungs gives expected cost-to-completion and names the bottleneck to fix first.

Separately, the challenge contract is a defect-escape problem: if a challenge detects a defect with probability d, k independent challenges leave escape probability (1-d)^k. That turns 'adversarial challenge is a contract' into a quantified assurance claim. The correlation caveat is the most important part and must not be buried: challenges sharing a model or a prompt are not independent, and the naive formula then overstates assurance, possibly badly. This is N-version programming's known failure mode (Littlewood and Miller 1989) reappearing as multi-challenge-same-model.
acceptance_criteria: Transition probabilities measured from the work log rather than assumed; bottleneck rung named; escape model stated with the independence assumption tagged [unverified] and its violation quantified where possible.
notes:

Both acceptance criteria ('transition probabilities measured from the work log', not assumed) are unreachable until Phase 2 dogfood runs land. Do not pick this bead expecting to execute it; the transition matrix cannot be fitted and a fitted-from-nothing matrix is exactly the defect this epic exists to remove.
close_reason: Pruned under the 2026-08-05 decision-theory demotion (construct-r67.20): RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md §7 already states the formalism and marks its conclusions pending data. Building the Markov model before any decision consumes it is modeling for its own sake — the wheel Gerald named. §7 stays as the formalism note; this bead dies.

title: Decision-science research pass: put the decision layer on a measured statistical footing
description:
Almost every load-bearing behavior in Construct is a decision under uncertainty (which domains an outcome implicates, when to spend a model call, whether a deliverable promotes past draft, when a phase gate has been passed), and almost all of them are governed by hand-chosen integers with prose justifications: MIN_SIGNAL=10, FULL_MATCH=7, keyword scores 3/7/10, concurrency 2, lease 15min, the intake confidence ramp 0.55/0.72/0.82/0.92, the 0.15 miss target, 'three to five external users'.

The trigger is a defect in the project's own measurement discipline. The fresh corpus holds 10 outcomes carrying 10 expected labels. The reported miss rate of 0.300 is 3/10, whose Wilson 95% interval contains the 0.15 target. The conclusion recorded in construct-4jq and reported on 2026-08-03 ('the target is not met, and the chosen design cannot reach it') is not supported at that sample size. That is commitment 15 failing on the project's own metrics: the corpora are measured honestly and then reasoned about as if precise.

Produces RESEARCH-DECISIONS.md as a third standing document alongside STRATEGY.md and GLOSSARY.md, covering the whole decision surface: implication map and routing scoring, escalation policy, intake confidence, completion ladder and promotion, run coordination, corpus and eval design, and the STRATEGY.md phase gates. Serves commitment 15 (no fabrication, applied to the system's own numbers) and commitment 16 (self-accountability).

STRATEGY.md is not edited in this pass. Target revisions are recommended with derivations and left to Gerald.

The lint exemption is narrowed from the whole tables directory to blanking 'keywords: [...]' arrays only — match keywords are the words USERS write in their documents and renaming them would break classification. value: Two false passes in one day (2026-08-13) from the same shortcut: writing a structural check, passing its own fixtures, and assuming it fires on real output. (1) namesAnOwner passed 'Owner: [unowned] — security/platform admin owns assertRecentReauth' because the whole-value test saw a long string; fixed by reading the head of the attribution (construct-kpkv.5). (2) The same check then PASSED a real deliverable whose decision-owner slot said no owner is named, because two narrow action-owner attributions existed elsewhere in the document — the check asks 'is an owner named' and the rubric line says 'is the DECISION owner named' (construct-k5jf). Rule: after landing any structural gate, run it against real recorded deliverables from the store, not only fixtures, and check the verdict is the one you intended — a gate that passes what it was built to fail is worse than no gate, because the promotion state now reads as cleared. Deliverables are readable via listTasks + latestDraft on the store at resolvePaths().dataDir.

Gerald's standing expectation for Construct (2026-08-13): it is a contributor on the team, not a reviewer that reports what it noticed. A run that identifies work it had the material, licence and context to do, and hands it back instead, has failed even when every claim in it is true and cited. Applies to every ask, not just strategy documents — the failure class showed up at three levels at once: a role's open-questions slot, the composition's uncovered list, and the run itself. When reviewing construct output, judge it on whether the remaining work got done, not on whether the gaps got named accurately.

The compose closing round (src/kernel/run/closing.ts, landed bd3febfe) exists because a named gap was a dead end. Three constraints are load-bearing and must survive any change to it. (1) A closing answer is NEW text from a fresh dispatch, so it passes the challenges its author's own brief already owed (screenClosedAnswers) — the earlier reasoning that it needs no screen because 'nothing arranged it' was wrong: the composed document's whole claim is that every line in it was checked, and one unchecked paragraph inherits the credibility of the checked ones beside it. (2) Gaps match verbatim (whitespace/case only); a fuzzy match lets a model answer an adjacent question and have the kernel file it as the answer to the real one. (3) A gap two roles answer differently is CONTESTED and both answers print — resolving by arrival order puts one side of a disagreement in the document under a single name. Also: the round can hide the very signal Gerald used to notice construct was stopping short, so what was closed, by whom, and what still stands must always print.

A recorded constraint, mechanism, or blocker is a hypothesis with a date and a setup attached, never a law. Before treating one as blocking, re-derive it: name the conditions it was measured under, test the cheapest alternative path, and amend the record with what turned out true. 'It always worked this way' licenses nothing. (Gerald, 2026-08-20, from the credential unblock: the recorded launch-time-only secrets mechanism was right about the mechanism but wrong as a permanent blocker — the missing piece was a key that did not yet exist.)

This repo's comments assert invariants, so a comment is a claim that can be false, and a false one is a defect — treat it as failing code, not as prose. Two caught in one session on 2026-08-13 by rereading new code adversarially before running the gate. (1) closing.ts claimed a second role's contradicting answer 'stays in the record so nothing is lost'; it was dropped from output entirely — fixed by making contested gaps a first-class result that prints both answers. (2) A design comment argued closing answers need no screen 'because nothing arranged them'; true and irrelevant, since the composed document's whole claim is that every line was checked — fixed by holding closing answers to the challenges their author's brief already owed. Practice that found both: after writing a module, read each comment and ask what observable behaviour would be different if it were false, then check that behaviour exists. Write the tests from the comments.

When changing a rule in this repo, grep for hand-rebuilt copies of it before calling the change done — they exist, they are silent, and they were each written by someone reasonable. Adding reader-acceptance lines to challengesFor() surfaced two: scripts/generate-org-map.mjs rebuilt the declared set as [...SPINE_CHALLENGES, legal-issue-spot] and had therefore been publishing an org map that omitted strongest-objection for months, and tests/kernel/run/spine-challenges.test.ts asserted a third hand-built copy. The fix in both cases is to ask the rule (export it, call it) rather than to update the copy. A test that asserts an exact list it assembled itself is not testing the rule, it is testing that two hand-copies agree. Same class as the glossary/org-map parity lints already in the gate.
